seo.title: DPDP-Aligned AI Data Handling Assessment | VipraTech
seo.description: Technical assessment of how fintech AI systems handle personal data: data-flow mapping, erasure and retention tests, and a DPDP gap register for your DPO.

problem.intro: AI features copy personal data into places privacy programmes were not built for: prompts sent to model providers, conversation logs, vector stores, evaluation datasets and call transcripts. Under the DPDP Act 2023, a fintech remains responsible as data fiduciary for that data wherever its processors handle it. Most teams cannot yet show where it goes, how long it stays or whether an erasure request reaches it.

pain_points.title: Unmapped AI data flows
pain_points.detail: Records of processing cover core systems but not prompt logs, embeddings, provider-side retention or evaluation datasets.

pain_points.title: Purpose creep
pain_points.detail: Data collected for KYC or support gets reused to tune or evaluate models without checking it against the purpose stated in the notice.

pain_points.title: Erasure that stops at the database
pain_points.detail: Deleting a customer from core systems leaves copies in vector indexes, caches, transcripts and fine-tuning sets.

pain_points.title: Unreviewed vendor terms
pain_points.detail: Model provider terms on retention, training use and hosting location are not checked against your obligations or RBI's payment data storage expectations.

solution.overview: We assess your AI features against the data handling duties in the DPDP Act 2023, working alongside your DPO and legal counsel. We trace personal data through each AI system: what is collected, which prompts and tools receive it, where it is logged, embedded, cached or sent to a provider, how long it is kept and who can access it. We test the controls instead of only reading policies: redaction, access controls, retention jobs and whether a seeded erasure request removes data from every AI store. You receive a data-flow map, a gap register mapped to DPDP obligations with owners and priorities, and an evidence pack your compliance team can maintain.
capabilities: Data-flow mapping across prompts, retrieval indexes, logs, transcripts, evaluation sets and model providers
Notice and consent review: whether AI uses match the purposes customers were told about
Control testing for redaction, access, retention and deletion, including a seeded erasure request
Model provider and processor review covering retention, training use and hosting location
Breach-readiness check on detecting and scoping a leak from an AI system
Gap register and evidence pack mapped to DPDP obligations for your DPO

workflow.title: Scope AI systems
workflow.detail: We list AI features, internal copilots and vendor tools that touch personal data, with an owner for each.

workflow.title: Trace data flows
workflow.detail: Through interviews, configuration review and logs, we map personal data from collection to every AI store and processor.

workflow.title: Assess against obligations
workflow.detail: Each flow is checked for notice and consent, purpose, minimisation, security safeguards, retention and data principal rights.

workflow.title: Test controls
workflow.detail: We test redaction, access and retention, and run a seeded erasure request to see which stores it reaches.

workflow.title: Record gaps
workflow.detail: Gaps are logged with a risk rating, an owner and a practical fix, then reviewed with your DPO and counsel.

workflow.title: Assemble the evidence pack
workflow.detail: The data-flow map, test results and decisions are packaged for your DPO to maintain and report from.

faqs.q: Is this a legal compliance audit?
faqs.a: No. It is a technical assessment that gives your DPO and counsel evidence of how AI systems actually handle personal data. Legal interpretation and sign-off stay with them.

faqs.q: Do model providers' no-training settings solve this?
faqs.a: They help with one part. Prompt and log retention, hosting location, your own vector stores and transcripts, and erasure across all of them still need checking.

faqs.q: How do you handle the phased DPDP Rules timelines?
faqs.a: We map gaps against each obligation and record the dates your counsel has set internally, so the remediation plan follows your compliance calendar rather than a generic one.

faqs.q: Can you cover GDPR at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes, for European customers or operations. Many controls overlap, and we note where GDPR requirements such as lawful bases, transfer rules or data protection impact assessments differ from DPDP.
